events.reason: Right leg weakness after motorcycle crash

conditions.label: Brown-Séquard syndrome
conditions.note: Right hemicord contusion at T10, motorcycle crash

reports.text:
MRI THORACIC SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Indication: motorcycle crash, right leg weakness, sensory level.
Technique: sagittal and axial T1, T2 and STIR sequences.
Findings: T2 hyperintense signal within the right half of the spinal cord at T10, consistent with cord contusion. No intramedullary hemorrhage. Cord is not compressed. Vertebral body heights and alignment are maintained; no fracture. No epidural hematoma. Posterior ligaments intact. Remaining cord signal normal.
reports.conclusion: Right hemicord contusion at T10. No fracture, compression or ligamentous injury.

documents.title: Outside ED Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY MEDICINE NOTE (outside hospital)
DOS 06/22/2026, arrival 17:45, trauma alert

CC: weak right leg after motorcycle crash.

HPI: 34M brought in after a motorcycle crash this afternoon. Known to us from crashes and a hand injury in 2024-25 (L leg embolectomy and R hand fasciotomy Dec 2024; L hand injection injury June 2025). Complains his right leg is weak and he can't feel it when it's touched.

Meds: none. NKDA.
FH: father with HTN, mother with hypothyroidism.
SH: former smoker (quit 2024). EtOH socially, 2-3 drinks/wk. Spray painter.

Vitals: see flowsheet.

Neuro: alert and oriented. Arms: full strength and normal sensation both sides. RLE strength 3/5. Proprioception and vibration diminished in the right leg. Light touch decreased on the right from T10 down. Pain and temperature preserved on the right, reduced on the left from T12 down. Reflexes normal throughout. Denies bowel or bladder incontinence.
Rest of trauma survey without injury.

Labs: CBC wnl. Lytes wnl. Tox screen negative.
MRI T-spine: right hemicord contusion at T10, no fracture.

MDM: Picture is a Brown-Sequard syndrome at T10 from a right hemicord contusion - ipsilateral weakness and dorsal column loss, contralateral spinothalamic loss two levels lower. Spine surgery consulted. Admit to trauma.

Dx: Traumatic Brown-Sequard syndrome, T10.
Dispo: admit, trauma surgery.

documents.title: Outside Hospital Discharge Summary - Trauma
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
TRAUMA SERVICE DISCHARGE / TRANSFER SUMMARY
Admitted 06/22/2026. Transferred to inpatient rehabilitation 06/26/2026.

Principal dx: Brown-Sequard syndrome at T10 (right hemicord contusion) after motorcycle crash.

Course: Spine surgery reviewed the MRI: no fracture, no instability, no compression. Nonoperative management, no brace needed. Enoxaparin for DVT prophylaxis while inpatient. PT and OT from day 1; up with a walker by day 3. Right leg strength unchanged early, improving slightly at transfer. Voiding on his own, bowels moving, no incontinence.

Allergies: NKDA.
Home medications: none.

Transfer: acute inpatient rehabilitation.

documents.title: Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
REHABILITATION DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 06/26/2026 - Discharge 07/17/2026 (21 days)

Rehab dx: Incomplete thoracic spinal cord injury, Brown-Sequard pattern, T10, traumatic.

Program: 3 hours a day of PT and OT. Gait training, right leg strengthening, balance work, stairs.

At discharge: right leg strength 4/5 throughout. Walks household and community distances with a single-point cane, stairs with a rail. Independent in dressing, bathing and toileting. Bladder emptying normally, no retention; bowels regular, continent. Skin intact.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medication: acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs every 8 hrs as needed.

Plan: outpatient PT three times a week. PM&R clinic in about 4 weeks. No driving or motorcycle until cleared. Off work; return to be decided at PM&R follow-up. PCP visit within a week.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
TCM call. Pt home since Fri 7/17 after 3 weeks inpatient rehab for a spinal cord injury (motorcycle crash 6/22).

Says he is getting around the apartment with the cane, managing the stairs slowly. No falls. Peeing and bowels normal. Takes acetaminophen once or twice a day, that's his only med. First outpatient PT eval is Wednesday afternoon. A friend is driving him for now.

Reviewed when to call: new weakness, numbness creeping up, trouble urinating, a fall. Appt with PCP 7/22 at 10:40. Trauma summary already in chart; rehab discharge summary came in this morning.

events.reason: Hospital and rehab follow-up, spinal cord injury

documents.title: Hospital Follow-Up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit.

34M, third serious injury in 18 months. Motorcycle crash 6/22: right hemicord contusion at T10 on MRI with a Brown-Sequard pattern, no fracture. Trauma admit 6/22-6/26, nonoperative per spine. Inpatient rehab 6/26-7/17. All records reviewed.

He walked in with a cane. Right leg tires and feels heavy by the end of the day. Feels his right foot "isn't where I think it is" sometimes. No falls. Bladder and bowels normal. Sleep ok. Mood: frustrated about being out of work, not down. Acetaminophen 1-2x/day, enough. PT eval is this afternoon.

Meds: acetaminophen 1000 mg q8h prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal, weight steady. Alert, cheerful enough. Arms: normal strength, sensation and reflexes. RLE: 4/5 hip flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion. LLE 5/5. Position sense reduced at the right great toe, vibration reduced right ankle. Pinprick and cold reduced left leg. Reflexes normal and symmetric. Walks steadily with a single-point cane. Skin intact over sacrum and heels.

PHQ-9: 4.

A/P
1. Brown-Sequard syndrome T10, traumatic, improving. Continue outpatient PT 3x/week, PM&R follow-up mid-August. Fall precautions reviewed.
2. Pain: acetaminophen as is.
3. Mood: PHQ-9 4. Normal frustration, will keep checking.
4. Work: out of work per rehab. He'll bring in the short-term disability paperwork from his employer's insurer.
5. No riding or driving until cleared.

RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner if he slips.

documents.title: PM&R Clinic Letter
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

I saw Victor Morales in clinic on 08/13/2026, four weeks after discharge from our inpatient unit for an incomplete T10 spinal cord injury with a Brown-Sequard pattern (06/22/2026).

He is in outpatient PT three times weekly. Right leg strength is 4/5. He no longer needs the cane in the house and uses it outdoors and on uneven ground. Bladder and bowel function remain normal. No falls. Pain controlled with acetaminophen as needed.

Plan: continue PT with endurance and balance goals. Not yet ready for the standing and booth work of his job; we will reassess return to work in about 6 weeks. Still no motorcycle or driving.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: acetaminophen prn.

Sincerely,
Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
